observed_source_defect.mechanism: Both canonical user sessions were created and attached through one shared tmux server socket name, clayverse. Authentication selected the initial target session, but the tmux client remained connected to the same server that contained both canonical sessions.
affected_contracts: Clerk-authenticated identity must remain bound through PTY runtime

counterhypothesis: Targeting a canonical tmux session with attach-session -t is sufficient isolation even when both sessions share one tmux server.
rationale: tmux clients connect to a server through a socket and server-scoped commands can target sessions in that server. Therefore the security boundary should not rely on the initial session target when the authenticated user must not gain a route to the peer user's terminal perspective.

repair.mechanism: Derive a distinct tmux -L socket/server name from the already-validated canonical user binding and use it consistently for has-session, new-session and attach-session.

regression_obligations_added: canonical users resolve to distinct tmux server sockets
session creation uses only the bound user's tmux server
PTY attachment uses only the bound user's tmux server
external_primary_evidence: tmux official GitHub wiki: Getting Started - clients connect to the tmux server through its socket
tmux official GitHub wiki: Advanced Use - separate servers may be selected with -L and can be used for complete isolation

parallel_work.gateway_lane: Current main already contains the separate WebSocket protocol/input-bound hardening from PR #419 lineage; this candidate changes terminal_sessions.py only and does not duplicate terminal_gateway.py.

execution_evidence.note: Source inspection, test definitions and GitHub writes are not executable ClayVerse runtime evidence.
